# 元始天尊說玄微妙經-六朝

**ID:** KR5a0060
**Custom ID:** ZB5a0060

**Editions:** SJB, ZHDZ

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A seven-folio Six-Dynasties Shàngqīng scripture containing one of several versions of the *Wǔdǒu sānyī* 五斗三一 ("Five Bushels and Three Ones") method — also called *Wǔdǒu nèiyī* 五斗內一 — a variant practice of *shǒuyī* 守一 ("Keeping the One"). The present method is given in the biography of Sū Lín 蘇林 as the *Zhōujūn kǒujué* 周君口訣 ("Oral Formula of Lord Zhōu"; cf. [YJQQ 49](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a1032) 11b), Lord Zhōu being Zhōu Jǐtōng 周季通 (Zǐyáng zhēnrén 紫陽真人, the "author" of Sū Lín's biography). The practice is said to have been known to Sīmǎ Jìzhǔ 司馬季主 (d. c. 170 BCE) and to other masters of antiquity, including Master Zhāng of Hándān 邯鄲張先生 (DZ 1016 *Zhēngào* 10.6a–b).

The text divides into two parts: **(i)** folios 1a–2b: a method to rise up to the Dipper, escorted by the Three Ones, the gods of the Three Cinnabar Fields (*dāntián* 丹田) — this portion is also found in *[DZ 1314 Dòngzhēn tàishàng sùlíng dòngyuán dàyǒu miàojīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a1314)* 38a–b and 39a–41b. **(ii)** folios 2b–7b: different methods concerning the Three Ones coming out of the Cinnabar Fields or coming down from the Dipper, spewing coloured *qì*. The same text is reproduced, in much condensed form, in *[DZ 1404 Shàngqīng tàijí zhēnrén shénxiān jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a1404)*.

**Abstract**

Isabelle Robinet, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 1:190–191 (§1.B.2, Shàngqīng), dates the text to the Six Dynasties. The most complete version of the method is found in *[YJQQ Yúnjí qīqiān 雲笈七籤](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a1032)* 49.11a–17b, with cognate versions in *[DZ 765 Shàngqīng Jīnquè Dìjūn wǔdǒu sānyī tújué 上清金闕帝君五斗三一圖訣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0765)* and *[DZ 140 Shàngqīng wòzhōngjué 上清握中訣](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5a/KR5a0140)* 2.2a–4b and 3.3a–5a. The frontmatter brackets composition notBefore 420 / notAfter 589, with dynasty 六朝. No author is attributed.
